credential_awarded.value: PMH-BC (Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse – Board Certified)

accreditation.value: Accredited by the Accreditation Board for Specialty Nursing Certification (ABSNC)

year_launched.note: ANCC does not publish a specific launch year for PMH-BC on the certification page. The credential replaced legacy RN-BC labeling for psychiatric-mental health nursing under ANCC's portfolio. Set to null rather than guess.

eligibility.value: Hold a current, active RN license in a US state/territory (or legally recognized equivalent in another country); two years of full-time RN practice; minimum 2,000 hours of clinical practice in psychiatric-mental health nursing within the last 3 years; 30 hours of continuing education in psychiatric-mental health nursing within the last 3 years.

exam_format.value: Computer-based test at Prometric centers; 150 questions (125 scored + 25 unscored pretest); 3-hour time limit; available year-round during a 120-day testing window after eligibility approval.

passing_score.value: Scaled score of 350 on a 0–500 scale (ANCC standard scaled passing score for board certifications).
passing_score.note: ANCC uses a uniform scaled passing score of 350 across its board certifications per the ANCC Certification Handbook.

pass_rate_2025.note: First-time test takers, 2025 ANCC Certification Data. Listed as 'Psychiatric-Mental Health Nursing' under RN Specialty Nursing.

renewal_ce_hours.value: 75 contact hours of continuing education in psychiatric-mental health nursing; at least 60 of the 75 must be formally approved CE (e.g., ANCC-accredited or AMA PRA Category 1).

renewal_pd_categories.value: Must complete at least 1 of 8 professional development categories: academic credits, presentations/lectures, publications/research, precepting students, professional service, practice hours (1,000+ in specialty), or re-examination (in addition to the 75 CE hours).

salary_context.value: BLS OEWS May 2024 — psychiatric/substance-abuse hospital RNs earn approximately $98,680 mean annual wage (vs ~$94,480 general RN mean). Range roughly $63,720 (10th pctl) to $132,680 (90th pctl).

tco_effective_date.note: Test Content Outline effective date; PDF was updated 2025-08-28 for web posting but content effective 2024-09-16.

blueprint.subtopics: Developmental stages (Erikson, Piaget); physiological causes of psychiatric symptoms (UTI, thyroid dysfunction); psychiatric disorders (thought, mood, neurocognitive, personality, addictions); coping/defense mechanisms; assessment tools (mental status exam, safety risk assessment, trauma history, diagnostic studies).

Client-centered care (strengths-based, client-stated goals, support network); educational concepts (motivation, readiness, group dynamics); cultural competence (gender-sensitive care, religious beliefs, ethnicity, SES); communication barrier management (cognition, literacy, language, vision); treatment planning (SMART goals, interdisciplinary interventions).

Treatment modalities (recovery model, trauma-informed care, CBT); integrative interventions (mindfulness, relaxation, aromatherapy); neurostimulation (TMS, ECT); care coordination; therapeutic environment (milieu, safety); therapeutic communication (active listening, motivational interviewing); medication management (reconciliation, adverse reactions, lab values); psychoeducational group facilitation; health promotion; emergent situation and crisis management.

Legal/ethical considerations (self-determination, informed consent, documentation); process improvement (quality variances, serious reportable events); outcome measurement, ongoing assessment (symptom reduction), and care-plan revision.

common_confusions.credential: PMHNP-BC (Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioner – Board Certified)
common_confusions.scope: Advanced practice nurse practitioner (APRN) credential across the lifespan; requires master's/DNP in psychiatric NP track. Distinct from PMH-BC, which is an RN-level specialty certification.

common_confusions.credential: PMHCNS-BC (Psychiatric-Mental Health Clinical Nurse Specialist – Board Certified)
common_confusions.scope: Adult or Child/Adolescent Psychiatric-Mental Health Clinical Nurse Specialist credentials. ANCC retired initial testing for these but maintains renewals. Different scope from RN-level PMH-BC.
Older labeling convention; ANCC has standardized this RN specialty credential under the PMH-BC label.

discrepancies.resolution: Use 150 per ANCC primary source (PMH-BC Test Content Outline effective 2024-09-16 and certification page state 150 questions / 3 hours). certs.js entry of 175 should be reconciled in a follow-up commit.

recent_changes.note: Current 4-domain blueprint (Assessment/Diagnosis 22%, Planning 21%, Implementation 46%, Evaluation 10%) was issued with TCO updated 2025-08-28 for web posting.

recent_changes.change: ANCC Certification Renewal Handbook effective September 10, 2025
recent_changes.note: 75 CE hours within the 5-year cycle, with 60 of those formally approved, plus one of eight professional-development categories.
